title: NOURISH Study- Nutritional Outcomes and Underlying Risk Investigation in Supportive Head and Neck Cancer Care
summary: Malnutrition and metabolic disturbances are common in head and neck cancer patients, often caused by treatment-related side effects such as dysphagia, mucositis, and taste changes, leading to weight loss, muscle wasting, and micronutrient deficiencies. The NOURISH study is a 12-month prospective observational study assessing body composition, inflammatory and micronutrient markers (vitamins, trace elements, omega-3 index), and functional measures. It aims to identify risk factors for malnutrition and guide potential targeted nutritional interventions.

interventions.name:
The study focuses on baseline nutritional assessment and longitudinal follow-up across 
defined treatment stages. A possible follow-up interventional study may be subsequently 
designed, if we identify actionable deficiencies and meaningful associations.

Type: Prospective, observational, multi-

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion Criteria (All Groups)
- Histologically confirmed HNC (squamous or related malignancy).
- Ongoing or planned treatment matching one of the study groups.
- Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG 0–2.
- Written informed consent; ability to undergo BIA, blood sampling, and questionnaires.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion Criteria (All Groups)
- Severe uncontrolled infection or comorbidity interfering with participation.
